metadata.evaluation_name: A third test, and every number rechecked
metadata.description: Two-part evaluation over the two iteration-1 reservoir-sampling experiments. PART A adds the published L1 identity / collision tester (Acharya-Daskalakis-Kamath arXiv:1507.05952; Diakonikolas-Kane-Nikishkin arXiv:1410.2266; collision-tester optimality Diakonikolas-Gouleakis-Peebles-Price) as a THIRD detector column beside the first-order max-deviation test and pairwise co-inclusion, and converts the result into a sample-complexity / state-complexity separation rather than a claim. PART B machine-recomputes every number the draft prints from the two full_method_out.json artifacts. PART C runs the validity checks a reviewer runs next. PART D constructs a distributed-merge defect whose per-item marginals are correct by construction.

verdict.part_A: BRANCH_1_TESTER_DETECTS (with a qualification the plan did not anticipate): the L1 identity/collision tester DOES detect the blind-spot samplers at T=1e6 despite having no worst-case guarantee there -- overall recall 0.969 on 32 degenerate runs with a 0.000 false-alarm rate on 48 provably-correct ones -- because their supports are tiny and the collision count is astronomically above the uniform expectation binom(T,2)/C(1000,10) = 1.9e-12. The qualification: detection is governed by lambda = binom(T,2)*||p||_2^2, NOT by L1 distance, so PAIR-LOCK -- equally far in L1 but with support C(500,5) = 2.55e11 and lambda = 1.96 -- is caught on only 0.875 of its seeds, at exactly the exp(-lambda) = 0.141 miss rate a Poisson(1.96) collision count predicts. Both branches are therefore realised within a single panel, at the same L1 distance.
verdict.part_A_matched_panel: On the 18 matched cells with exact-rational ground truth the L1 tester scores accuracy 1.000 / recall 1.000 / false alarm 0.000, against first-order 0.833/0.667, anytime all-prefix 0.833/0.667 (IDENTICAL to the final-reservoir first-order test, and missing the SAME three S5-CIRC cells -- the blindness is structural, not a power problem), and pairwise 1.000/1.000.
verdict.part_A_reframing: The honest separation among the three detectors is NOT about statistical power but about STATE, STREAMING-COMPATIBILITY, LOCALITY and WORST-CASE GUARANTEE. The first-order test keeps O(n) counters, is streaming, and never detects a defect whose first-order marginals are exact. Pairwise co-inclusion keeps O(n^2) counters, is streaming with memory independent of T, detects every blind-spot sampler in this run, and LOCALISES the defect by naming the item pairs that never co-occur. The L1 identity/collision tester needs Theta(sqrt(C(n,k))/eps^2) samples for a worst-case eps-far alternative and O(min(T,D)) memory to hold the distinct-sample table; it is extremely powerful against the SPECIFIC low-support alternatives here because their L2 norm is huge, but it gives no locality and its guarantee does not cover spread-out defects at any affordable T.
verdict.part_B: 18 printed numbers checked: 8 MATCH, 9 MISMATCH, 1 UNAVAILABLE. The measured error rate on printed numbers is therefore 0.500, and one headline claim has no executed support at all.
verdict.part_C1: EXECUTED. Co-inclusion calibration re-derived from an exactly uniform k-subset oracle at T = 2e+05 trials per run, null_B = 40 max-deviation and 16 co-inclusion null replicates per cell, over a 48-cell (n,k) sweep plus 4 fully calibrated cells. (i) THE NOMINAL RULE IS MIS-CALIBRATED, but the right evidence is not a single run: the sweep produces only 1 nominal false alarm on Algorithm R -- the provably uniform sampler -- and it is at n = 200, k = 40 (k/n = 0.20, p = 3.8e-08), which is the answer to the plan's question 'what is the smallest (n,k) at which the nominal rule first false-alarms' -- smallest both by k and by k/n on this grid. (ii) The DECISIVE quantity is the simulated null: the co-inclusion chi-square is over-dispersed relative to the nominal chi-square(df) reference by a factor of up to 3.45 in standard deviation (its bins are negatively correlated, which the nominal reference ignores), and its mean sits up to 1.0075 x df. Referring the nominal p < 1e-6 rule to that simulated null gives an IMPLIED false-alarm rate on a provably uniform sampler of up to 0.306 (at n = 2000, k = 100), and 3 of 4 calibrated cells are mis-calibrated by that test. So the declared deviation is justified -- just not by the single p = 7.9e-16 run the artifact quoted, whose cell gives p = 0.267 here. (iii) The CALIBRATED own-null rule (z >= 5 against the cell's own simulated null) separates the correct samplers from the broken ones with NO overlap: max z among correct = 1.817, min z among broken = 2.652e+04, a gap of 2.652e+04 -- four to six orders of magnitude, on every calibrated cell.
verdict.part_C1_caveat: The declared method deviation rested on a SINGLE run of Algorithm R at n=2000, k=100 giving a nominal p = 7.9e-16. In this re-derivation that single-run false alarm is NOT reproducible: re-running the same cell with the same seed but a different trial-chunk size (and hence a different partition of the same PCG64 stream) gives p = 0.267, while the sweep's only nominal false alarm lands at n=200, k=40 (k/n = 0.20, p = 3.8e-08). A single-run nominal p is therefore not a sound basis for declaring the rule mis-calibrated. The decisive quantity is the SIMULATED null of the co-inclusion chi-square, generated by an exactly uniform k-subset oracle that shares no code path with the sampler under audit; it is reported per calibrated cell in the calibration_and_sign_reversal dataset under metadata_part = C1_nominal_rule_miscalibration. The deviation itself stands on stronger ground regardless: the calibrated own-null rule separates correct from broken samplers with no overlap, so no verdict in either artifact depends on the nominal rule.
verdict.part_C2: MECHANISM_CONFIRMED. The sign reversal is real and mechanistic: 3 blind-spot samplers (S5e, S5g, S6sys) score BETTER (smaller max deviation from k/n) than Algorithm R on the field's standard first-order test at n=1000, k=10, T=1e+06. Simulating the statistic directly -- max over m effective bins rather than max over n = 1000 items, R = 2000 replicates per design, each sampler's effective bin count derived from its OWN support structure rather than assumed to be n/k -- predicts the shift for all 3 of 3 samplers INSIDE the simulated 95% interval: S5e (n/k = 1000/10 = 100 bins) predicted shift -6.86e-05 in [-1.06e-04, -3.09e-05], observed -6.05e-05; S5g (n/2 = 1000/2 = 500 bins) predicted shift -1.96e-05 in [-5.25e-05, 1.38e-05], observed -2.19e-05; S6sys (n/k = 1000/10 = 100 bins) predicted shift -6.86e-05 in [-1.06e-04, -3.09e-05], observed -5.00e-05. The analytic Gumbel shrinkage sqrt(2 ln m)/sqrt(2 ln n) gives 0.8165 for the m = n/k = 100 designs, matching the measured ratio to within 0.043 relative. IMPORTANT: PAIR-LOCK (S5g) locks items into n/2 = 500 pairs, not n/k = 100 blocks, so its effective bin count is 5x larger than BLOCK-LOCK's and its predicted shrinkage is correspondingly smaller. Assuming n/k for all three would mis-predict S5g. S5-CIRC is listed in the same table with 1000 effective bins (its first-order marginals are exactly uniform at every prefix, so it has no block structure to shrink the max over) and therefore no predicted shift to test.
verdict.part_C3: 12 references checked against authoritative records. 7 VERIFIED as printed, 2 CORRECTED, 2 flagged NON_PEER_REVIEWED (reference [11], Breitner's blog post -- attributional only, since the parallel experiment re-derives its closed form independently -- and Lumbroso's arXiv preprint), and 1 UNRESOLVED: reference [25] is printed with year 2025 against a DOI in the 2026 IEEE Trans. Inform. Theory volume range, and no exact DOI string was supplied, so no unique record could be resolved -- the search steps taken are recorded rather than a guessed year. Per-reference rows, with canonical record and source URL, are in the reference_hygiene dataset.
verdict.part_D: EXECUTED. The constructed merge defect has per-item marginals identical to the correct merge BY CONSTRUCTION (both exactly k/(n1+n2) = 0.01), verified empirically. first-order recall 0.00 (false alarm 0.00), pairwise co-inclusion recall 1.00 (false alarm 0.00). DECISIVE ADDITION: the L1 identity/collision tester ALSO misses it -- 0 collisions under both merges -- because the defective merge keeps a constant fraction of the full support, so it is far in L1 but has essentially the uniform L2 norm. This is the spread-out defect that the worst-case Theta(sqrt(D)/eps^2) bound warns about and that no affordable T reaches, and it leaves pairwise co-inclusion as the only detector of the three that finds it.

preregistered_part_A_branches.branch_1_tester_detects: The blind-spot samplers have support O(n) or C(n/2,k/2), so ||p||_2^2 is enormous relative to 1/C(n,k) and the expected collision count at T=1e6 is astronomically above the uniform expectation binom(T,2)/C(n,k) ~ 1.9e-12. Predicted BEFORE running.
preregistered_part_A_branches.branch_2_tester_has_no_power: The worst-case bound T = Theta(sqrt(C(1000,10))/eps^2) ~ 5e11 at eps=0.1 says the tester has no GUARANTEE at T=1e6; if it also had no power in practice the structural-blindness claim would be strengthened.

worst_case_versus_instance_specific.statement: At n=1000, k=10 the worst-case guarantee of the L1 tester needs T = c*sqrt(C(1000,10))/eps^2 with the measured c = 5.49: that is 2.82e+14 samples at eps = 0.1 and 2.82e+12 even at the blind spots' own eps = 1.0. The panel used T = 1e6. The worst-case requirement and the instance-specific behaviour therefore differ by 6.5 to 8.5 orders of magnitude, and BOTH statements are true: the tester has no guarantee at this T, and it detects these particular alternatives anyway because their L2 norm -- not their L1 distance -- is what it actually measures.

metadata.part_A_fragility_finding: The L1 collision tester's power against a low-support alternative is governed by lambda = binom(T,2)*||p||_2^2, the expected collision count, NOT by the L1 distance. BLOCK-LOCK, SYSTEMATIC and CIRC have lambda of 5e9, 5e9 and 5e8 and are detected on every seed. PAIR-LOCK is just as far in L1 (exact TV = 1 - C(500,5)/C(1000,10) = 0.999999999999) but its support C(500,5) = 2.55e11 gives lambda = 1.96, so the tester sees a Poisson(1.96) number of collisions and MISSES it whenever that count is zero -- which happened on 1 of the 8 seeds, against a predicted miss probability exp(-1.96) = 0.141. Calibrated pairwise co-inclusion flags the same sampler at z = 1078.6 on every seed. This is the sharpest statement of the separation: the identity tester's power tracks the L2 norm of the alternative, the co-inclusion test's power tracks the second-order marginals, and only the latter is what a broken reservoir sampler actually violates.

vendored_adaptations.change: the rejection loop's pass cap was raised from 200 to 200000
vendored_adaptations.why: per-pass acceptance is prod_{i<k}(1-i/n) ~ exp(-C(k,2)/n), which is 0.086 at (n,k)=(500,50) and (2000,100); with T=2e5 rows a 200-pass cap leaves duplicated rows unresolved and the function raised RuntimeError mid-run, which killed the first C1 attempt after the (2000,100) cell had already completed
vendored_adaptations.does_it_change_any_law: NO -- the sampler is the same rejection sampler (draw k indices with replacement, discard rows with a repeat), simply run to completion instead of being truncated; conditioning a with-replacement draw on distinctness leaves every k-subset equally likely, so the null it simulates is unchanged. The (1000,10) and (1000,50) cells, which the truncated version did clear, reproduce their nominal p-values exactly.

chunk_probe.interpretation: Algorithm R is provably uniform, so every small p here is a false alarm. If the p value swings by many orders of magnitude when only the trial-chunk size changes -- with the SEED held fixed -- then a single-run nominal p is an artifact of how the PCG64 stream is partitioned, not a property of the (n,k) cell, and cannot on its own justify declaring the nominal rule mis-calibrated.

scope_limits.limit: k capped at 100 and n at 5000
scope_limits.why: the dense co-inclusion accumulator materialises chunk*C(k,2) linearised pair indices; at k=200 that is 1e9 int64 entries (8 GB) per chunk. The trial-chunk size is scaled as 2e7/C(k,2) to keep the buffer bounded, and the chunk actually used is recorded, because the chunk turns out to matter (see metadata.chunk_probe).

scope_limits.limit: 4 cells rather than the full grid, with 40 max-deviation and 16 co-inclusion null replicates per cell
scope_limits.why: an own-simulated null costs one exactly-uniform k-subset oracle run per replicate, and the co-inclusion replicates dominate: at n=2000, k=100 the band alone takes 263 s at 16 co-inclusion replicates and 1620 s at the plan's 48 (measured -- a first attempt at 200/48 was abandoned after the vendored rejection sampler raised RuntimeError at (500,50), see metadata.vendored_adaptations). The budget was cut to 40/16 so all four cells complete; the quantities read off the band are its MEAN and SD, which 16 replicates estimate to within ~18% relative standard error -- far finer than the 4-to-6-order-of-magnitude separation being measured. The declared n=2000,k=100 cell is included.
eps = 0.02 would put T_90 at ~4e6 per grid point and ~1e9 draws per cell; the four eps values retained already pin the exponent of eps to -1.96..-2.11 and of D to 0.48..0.54.

200 is the smallest R for which an exact Monte-Carlo p-value can reach the 0.01 level (1/201 = 0.00498); the null collision count is 0 in every one of the 200 replicates, matching the analytic lambda = 1.9e-12.

There is no ARITHMETIC contradiction -- every condition, once translated to the same physical quantity, says the same thing: the certificate/deterministic rank is exact iff the ARRIVING ITEM's own index is divisible by k. But the SYMBOL i is bound to two different quantities across these files, which is a real convention hazard (exactly the kind of thing that produces off-by-one bugs if code is copied between the two conventions without renaming):
  (1) fibermap.py uses i = PREFIX SIZE everywhere (build_fiber, entropy_bracket, analyse_step all treat i as the size of the already-seen set [i], with the arriving item explicitly labelled i+1, and its accept probability convention elsewhere in the codebase for this i is k/(i+1)). Its divisibility conditions are written as k|(i+1) or equivalently k|(i-k+1).
  (2) E1/forced.py's OWN bit_budget function switches convention MID-FILE: its docstring explicitly redefines i as 'the arriving item index' (not the prefix used two functions earlier in forced_accept_check, where i again means the PREFIX, matching fibermap.py). bit_budget's divisibility condition is k|i with i = arriving item -- the SAME symbol i means prefix in forced_accept_check and arriving-item in bit_budget within one module.
  (3) E2/s1t.py and E2/candidates.py both consistently use i = ARRIVING ITEM INDEX (accept probability k/i, sources drawn from [i-1]), and write the divisibility condition as k|(i-k) (equivalently k|i, used directly by S5e's step_filter). This matches forced.py's bit_budget convention but NOT fibermap.py's convention.
  (4) E1/candidates.py has no divisibility condition to compare directly, but its accept(i,k) = Fraction(k, i) (candidates.py:41-42) shows it ALSO uses i = arriving item, i.e. even within experiment E1, fibermap.py's i-convention (prefix) disagrees with candidates.py's i-convention (arriving item) though the two modules are used together (candidates.py:28 imports fibermap and candidates.py's TableDriven sampler class reads fibermap's flow tables built with build_fiber(i,k) using i=prefix, while candidates.py's own evict(slots,i,k) signature receives i=arriving item -- so any code path that calls fibermap.build_fiber(i, k) using the i handed to evict() would silently be off by one, unless it is deliberately translated, which the surrounding code in fibermap.py's own analyse_cell/eviction_table wrappers appears to do by passing the prefix explicitly.)
